Their bill to repeal it: June 12, 2025

cut.why: Mid-video 'subscribe' ask breaks the flow right before the wages argument; cut it or move it to the end.

Jones Act plus the AMP and critics quotes plus the subsidy is about 35s of names, dates and quotes while the picture is a static Seattle map. Trim the AMP and Lee/McClintock detail here, since it is repeated at 620–631.
Price-gap stats (1922, 1950s, 1990s, 2019 tanker) are delivered as a list over barely changing visuals. Keep two of them.
The loop is explained, then recapped with a hedge at 287–305 ('wages are one factor', 'only partly supports'), then recapped again at 604–631. The hedge repeats itself and the picture is static.
Korea's GDP per person in 1962 and the Hyundai 'no experience' quote are slow, with a dull beige map and no motion.
The turtle-ship banknote lore is a tangent. It is 18s of 'we found no documents' over a static map, so cut it to one line.
Munseob Lee's list, then 'sources don't say', then the per-person output figures with a 'not in our sources' disclaimer is a homework-style hedge run. Shorten it.

About 105s of USTR bureaucracy: petition, findings, fee mechanics, China's objection, suspension and trade-group letter. It is document pages and globe, with the same two shots reused. Roughly halve it.
The scoreboard is a third recap: the 'what to watch' list, then the scoreboard, then the verdict, then supporters and critics again. About 45s over a nearly empty map. Merge into one conclusion.

Cold open is 34s of stats, then 'so why?', then a deadline, then a restart in Richmond. The Philadelphia/Korea tease and the Nov 9 deadline are both re-explained later. Cut to about 15s: the 0.04% vs China contrast, the question, then go.
The Robert E. Peary 4.5-day stunt is a throwaway trivia beat after the 122 to 39 day payoff. Drop it or fold it into one clause.
'Our read' about customers, then British government, Maritime Commission, governments in wartime says the same thing three times. One sentence is enough.

Jones Act section is about 57s of dense legislative history with three quoted advocacy lines, a bill date and then the subsidy, over a near-static map. Cut the Wesley Jones biography and quote only one side or none.
A mid-roll subscribe plug lands right before the main argument starts and kills momentum. Move it to the end or cut it.
The 4x tanker estimate, the wages line and the scale line are three separate beats on a visually empty green map. Compress.
The loop is narrated, captioned three times and then summarized again ('the record says something narrower... our emphasis is a position...'). Cut the 287 to 304 recap or merge it with the loop.
Two 'not in our sources' hedges plus a per-capita GDP stat with no visual payoff. Keep one hedge.
Fee mechanics ('up to five times a year', fee rates) are too detailed for the thesis, and the labels are cluttered.

China's objection, the 'in light of' trade deal, the 200+ group letter and the 'no extension' status are four stacked bureaucratic beats. The status is repeated again at 576. Trim to the suspension and the deadline.

The scoreboard recap restates the thesis, then supporters and critics are re-quoted verbatim from 142 to 170, then a Richmond tag-out. About 45s of repetition. Cut the supporters/critics recap and the 'No source measures' line, or shorten each to a clause.
The mid-roll 'subscribe' plea breaks the argument right before the 'wages' pivot. Move it to the end or cut it.
The Jones Act pro/con quotes, the repeal bill and the CDS intro are crammed into about 30s, and the pro/con is repeated at 620-631. Keep one line each now, or move the full debate to the close.
The loop is stated at 273-282, again at 287-299 ('narrower than wages'), and a third time in the 600s recap. Cut the 287-305 restatement to one sentence.
Two 'sources don't say' caveats back to back, plus a per-capita GDP stat that doesn't connect to ships. Merge them or shorten.
Fee mechanics (size-based, 5x a year) are dense, with two quoted USTR aims on screen as stacked bullets. Summarize in one line.
The trade-group letter, with its long quote, is minor and slows the run into Philadelphia.
The scoreboard and recap repeat the Jones Act pros and cons and the loop almost word for word. Cut about 20-25s, keeping the 'Our read' conclusion and the no-source-measures line.
The Richmond national-park epilogue and the next-video teaser run long, and the teaser is shown twice (narration plus caption).

transitions.why: The disclaimer caption (C01) lands over the globe in the first seconds of the hook and stays up for about 10s, so it fights the cold open.
The Philadelphia shot starts at 17–18s but the caption is not cleared. 'Owner announced plans' stays up through the 'Why so few ships?' title at 22–28s, so two messages overlap.
The hook jumps straight into a 1940 Richmond map with no cue that the video is going back in time. The 'November ninth' deadline is dropped and not revisited for 8 minutes.
Cut from the map to a dim film frame and an archival photo. The caption says '1944 newsreel' while the narration is about 1942–43 build times, and the film frame is nearly black.
After 'cargo to Vancouver' the map jumps to the Pacific Northwest with no caption or label for about 8s, and the Wesley Jones photo name overlaps the picture at 122s.
Seattle jumps to an unlabeled sandy map for the subsidy. The 15–25 ships bar appears at 178s, long after narration starts at 176s.
Hard jump from a sandy 1970s map to a green generic map with a tiny figure and the 'COMMON CLAIM' tag. The geography is unclear.
Jumps to a full US globe and a spinning Earth, then to Korea, with the map visuals unrelated to the 1962 GDP narration. The sudden move from the US to Korea is not signposted.
A sudden switch from the Korea map to a blank white document page for 12s, with a 'Which brings us to the present' line that has no visual setup.
The fee explanation sits on a Philadelphia map with 'Port of Philadelphia', which was never introduced. The viewer has no reason to expect Philadelphia here.
Three stretches of the recap are separate beats ('what to watch', then scoreboard, then verdict) with the same empty green map reused.
Philadelphia map is held while the question is asked, with the 'South Korean group' caption still up. The visual is about a different line than the narration.
Hard jump from the Philadelphia/deadline tease to Richmond 1940 with no bridge. The viewer has to guess why we are in California.
Subscribe plug interrupts the Jones Act/subsidy segment, then an abrupt pivot to 'the answer you'll often hear'.
Tone and visual reset to a green blank map with a tiny figure, as if a new video started.
Jump to a US/globe fly-over for South Korea's 1962 GDP, with no caption and no stat on screen.
Cut from the Korea map to a blank document page for the USTR petition. Unlabeled and abrupt, and the Korea payoff is never tied to China.
'And Philadelphia' returns to the same green map used for the trade-group letter. It is hard to tell the topic has changed.
Ending tag-out in Richmond overlaps the 'Next' caption with the map label. The final beat is weak.

The cold open starts on an unlabeled Richmond relief map while narration talks about 1943 and 'three ships a day'. The 0.04% / 'more than half' comparison at 5-17s is only a spinning globe with no chart or number.
The Philadelphia river map is shown while the narration says 'South Korean'. The C02 strip lingers to 29s, so the old caption sits under the new 'Why does America…' title.
A hard jump from the Philadelphia hook to Richmond. The deadline line at 28.6s is introduced and then never visually resolved.
A dark, nearly blank archive film frame for the 'Liberty was a slow cargo ship' line. The picture does not illustrate the narration.
A cut from Richmond to a Washington/Vancouver terrain map with no label for about 8s. The cargo-by-rail-to-Vancouver story is hard to follow.
A jump from the Seattle map to a blank Richmond-style map with a CDS caption. The subsidy, which is the point of the section, has no visual.
The 'wages' section reuses the Philadelphia river map with a tiny figure and no connection to wages. This is a hard topic switch with a generic visual.
A US globe, then a Korea globe, with a 1962 per-capita-output fact and no on-screen number. Then a cut to a Korean map. The 1962 stat is never shown.

A blank paper sheet, then a globe, then a document, then Philadelphia port at 463 while narration is about fees. Philadelphia then appears again at 528 as 'And Philadelphia', so the earlier use confuses.
The 'what to watch' list sits on an almost empty river map. The 'scoreboard' then jumps to the Richmond bay map.

empty.why: The opening frame is a bare terrain with no subject while the narration makes its biggest claim, so the hook has no striking visual.
The 'Why does America build so few ships?' title, the Philadelphia tag and the C02 caption all compete.
A dark, low-contrast film frame with the tiny archival caption at the bottom.
A pale map with one tiny shipyard icon during the '747 ships' stat, so the stat has no visual weight.
The 122/39/4.5-day labels, two bars, a ship and a ghost frame all show at once, with tiny text on a phone.
A bare terrain with no caption or label while the Jones/Alaska backstory is narrated.
A Seattle map with only a tag, then at 158s stacked quote tags and a source line crowd the lower-left.
The '15–25 ships/yr' label overlaps the top-left edge and its text is clipped.
A plain green map with one tiny figure for about 12s, with no caption.
The '99 ships' and 'wages (welders)' tags are tiny and low-contrast on a phone.
The Wages/Scale chips are tiny and the loop graphic is faint, then the picture darkens at 304s.
A beige Korea map with one small label while the Hyundai story is narrated.
No caption and a bare map for 'government set its own targets'.
A white document page with unreadable text and no caption for about 4s.
The document text is a blurred, unreadable scan with a tiny highlight.
Fee tags ($18 / $50 per net ton) overlap the ship and the 'Port of Philadelphia' label, with tiny text.
Several tags ($5B, 1.5→20, Philly Shipyard) stack in the middle of a busy aerial photo.
A green river map with a source line only, for about 20s of the 'what to watch' list.
The small scoreboard tag is the only content, and the wording at 620s fades out.
A bare map under the Critics caption, with nothing else on screen.
Opening is a flat relief map with a stray '43' tag and no caption or stat, while the strongest hook line is being spoken.
Disclaimer caption sits over the globe and is up 7s during the 0.04% stat. It is two lines of small text competing with the hook.
Globe with green rays shows 'China more than half' with no number or label on screen.
Richmond map is empty, with no caption for about 2s.
Sepia newsreel frames are nearly blank and dark, with little visible subject.
Near-empty terrain map, with a tiny ship icon and no caption.
Terrain map has no labels and no caption for 8s while the Alaska/Vancouver story is told.
Senator's name label sits off the photo at the edge, and the later text is tiny.
Two overlapping quote labels, a map pin and a 'Facts as of' badge crowd the map.
The two bar labels collide at the top-left ('5 ships/yr' overlaps '15-25 ships/yr').
Green map with a speck-sized figure and no content.
Empty green map with a nearly invisible wages tag while 8s of narration plays.
Tiny '99 ships' and wages labels are unreadable at 540p.
Wages/Scale chips in the corner are tiny, and the loop icons are indistinct.
Globe fly-over has no caption, and the narration is about a $107 GDP figure that is not shown.
Blank map with only the tiny source line.
Blank map, no label or caption.
Blank white document page with unreadable text. It shows nothing and has no caption for 4s.
Document page is blurry and the highlight is illegible.
Port of Philadelphia label, two fee labels and the badge are all on one map. It also looks wrong for a China fee story.
Source line wraps to two lines, and the long quote caption is dense.
Stacked $5B, 1.5 to 20 ships and 'Philly Shipyard' labels over the caption and a 'Facts as of' badge.
Watch-list map is empty, with no icons for the three things to watch.
Supporters caption fades in over a busy bay map and is hard to read.
Two-line 'Next' caption collides with the source line, and the 'Richmond Shipyard No. 3' label floats on the map.
A tiny '43' badge is stuck to the time stamp area. The source strip text is too small for a phone.
The disclaimer strip and the small source line stack at the bottom. The disclaimer is a long two-line sentence over a bright globe.
A rotating globe carries the Congress-versus-China 0.04% comparison with no numbers on screen.
The C02 caption is still up under the centered title question, and the Philadelphia label sits on the title.
A dark film frame with almost no readable content.
Three data labels, a place label, ship icons and a boxed overlay at the same time (59-67s). The 4½-day label is dim and tiny.
A bare terrain map with no labels for about 8s.
The 'Sen. Wesley L. Jones' label sits on the white photo edge with low contrast and wrapped text (122-130).
Two quote boxes plus the Seattle label and the 'Facts as of' tag on one map.
The two chart labels collide ('15-25 ships/yr' overlapped by '5 ships/yr') at the top-left, and are clipped.
A green map with only a tiny pin and a 'wages' tag for 237-257s. The cost-gap numbers are not shown.
The loop dots and the circle are unlabeled while three captions fire within 6s (C22-C24). The top-left pills 'Wages' / 'Scale' are tiny.
The pills fade out along with the caption, and the caption is dim.
The 'no experience, capital…' quote is two lines in small text over beige terrain. The 'Chung Ju-yung' label is tiny.
The 'LORE' label, the 500-won note label and document icons are stacked on a busy map before the LORE caption at 353.
A bare Korean map for about 5s with no label.
A faint ghost label at the top-left of the map, then a '$36,227' box. The sea-lane lines compete with it.
The caption and label fade out while still being read.
A blank beige paper sheet for 8s. The 'unions petition' caption is the only content.
Three fee labels, the Port of Philadelphia label and the 'Facts as of' tag in one map.
Stacked labels ($5B, Philly Shipyard, 1.5→20, June 2030) over the shipyard. The text is tiny and the labels overlap each other.
A bare river map for the 'what to watch' stretch. The numbered list is plain caption text only.
The caption is mid-fade and shows at low contrast.
The two-line next-video teaser sits over bright coastline, and the source line is very small.

R1: Cut the caption count from 66 to about 40 by dropping every caption that repeats the voice-over (C05, C08, C10, C11–C14, C16, C17, C19, C21–C24, C26, C28, C29, C31–C36, C38, C40, C43, C44, C47, C51, C54–C58, C60–C66). Keep the source, date, 'Our read', LORE, 'as of' and deadline lines.

Cut about 2.5–3 minutes: the subscribe ask, the Jones Act quote stack, the price-gap list, the loop recap and its hedge, the turtle-ship lore, and half the USTR fee detail. Collapse the three ending recaps (what to watch, scoreboard, verdict) into one 30s close.

Replace the empty green or beige maps and the blank document pages with a single clear visual per beat (one big number, one photo, one chart). Keep tags large enough to read on a phone and remove the stacked tags at 67s, 471s and 543s.
R2: Cut about 45 of the 66 captions' worth of echo: delete the ~30 flagged lines (all pure narration repeats, the three loop captions, C10/C11 against C09, C58/C60/C62/C64/C66). Keep every source, date, 'Our read' and LORE line. That lands around 36 captions. Then trim 90s of narration from the Jones Act, tanker-estimate, loop recap, China-fee and scoreboard sections.

Rebuild the cold open and the dead stretches: cut the opening to about 15s (0.04% vs China, then the question). Move the subscribe plug out of 198s. Fill the empty map frames at 2, 35, 110, 205, 237, 306, 326, 374, 423 and 576 with a number, photo, chart or key image, and replace the blank document pages at 423 and 455 with a readable highlighted excerpt.

Fix the clutter: stack at most one label plus one caption at a time. Hold the disclaimer to a single short line (C01) and don't run it over the hook. Separate the overlapping bars at 198s, the stacked tags at 471s and 551s, and the 640s ending. Raise the minimum size of the tiny map tags so they read at 540p.
R3: Cut captions from 66 to about 34-40. Drop every caption that restates the narration (C05, C08, C10-C13, C15, C16, C22-C24, C26, C28, C29, C31-C34, C36, C38, C40, C43, C44, C47, C51, C54, C58, C60, C62-C66). Keep all 'Our read' lines, C30 (LORE), the date and 'as of' lines, and the source lines (C09, C17, C18, C35, C45, C52). Show the 'sources don't say' caveats once each, as a short label.

Trim about 90-100s of repeated or low-value narration. Cut the subscribe plea (198-204), the loop restated at 287-305 (the 273-282 version already carries it), the fee mechanics (464-486), the trade-group letter (510-528) and the 592-631 recap, which repeats the Jones Act pro/con and the loop. This tightens the run and fixes the 'wages' dead zone.

Replace the empty or generic maps with real visuals. Show the 0.04% / '>50%' share as a bar or number in the first 20s. Put a chart on screen for the cost gap (20% → 2x → 3x → 4x) in 205-245. Give the 'what to watch' list real map markers, and set the long labels on stacked cards, not dotted over terrain. Drop the repeated Philadelphia map from 463 (fees) and 205 (wages), and enlarge small labels for a phone.
